children: DeepSeek's annualized revenue run rate has topped $1 billion, more than doubling in recent months as the Chinese AI startup converts surging model adoption into stronger monetization. The milestone strengthens DeepSeek's case ahead of a planned funding round and possible Shanghai listing, but it also highlights how far Chinese AI companies still trail the revenue scale of U.S. leaders such as microsoft
Chief Executive Liang Wenfeng disclosed the figure during a recent investor meeting, according to The Information. Reuters said it could not independently verify the report.

The growth was partly driven by substantial price increases. DeepSeek reportedly raised model pricing by 2.3 to 4.5 times, suggesting the company is testing how much pricing power its lower-cost AI strategy can support.

DeepSeek is now targeting a second funding round of 50 billion yuan, or about $7.45 billion, at a 500 billion yuan valuation by the end of October. The company is also preparing for a potential listing on Shanghai's STAR Market.

Importantly, DeepSeek is still prioritizing model development over near-term inference revenue. More than 70% of its computing capacity is being used to train new models, while less than 30% supports existing-model inference.

Earlier this month, DeepSeek launched V4.1-Flash, a new model built for faster inference, higher throughput and lower infrastructure requirements. DeepSeek says the model uses materially less memory and storage than its prior generation, potentially improving serving economics.
The key question is whether DeepSeek can keep scaling revenue after sharply raising prices without undermining the low-cost positioning that helped drive adoption.
Investors should watch pricing retention, inference demand and how quickly the company shifts compute capacity from training toward revenue-generating workloads.

The prospective $7.45 billion fundraising and possible IPO could give DeepSeek substantially more capital to compete, but the revenue gap remains large. Even at a $1 billion run rate, DeepSeek is still far below reported annualized revenue levels for OpenAI and Anthropic.
That makes the next phase less about proving technical relevance and more about demonstrating durable monetization at scale.

title: DeepSeek Sends Strong Signal Ahead of Funding Push
